analysis.title: Goldilocks Or Bond Rout? Goldman's 10 Charts For A Market With A 20% De-Rating Behind It
key_insights: Goldman's asset allocation team is overweight equities on 3-month and 12-month horizons, underweight credit on both, overweight cash for the next three months, and moves to overweight 10-year government bonds over 12 months. The stated stance is more focused on balance but constructive on equities.

Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator spent much of the year above +1 and fell to -0.5 in October. The drop is driven by the monetary policy factor (PC2), as markets priced a hiking Fed under Warsh, which pulled growth sentiment down with it.

Across 11 PC2 troughs since 2000, the S&P 500 recovered on average, which makes sharp monetary-policy drops usually buying opportunities. 2022 is the exception, and the current path tracked the 2022 path more closely than the average.

Global 12-month forward P/E ratios have fallen about 20% while prices held up, because earnings carried the market. Dividend yield plus one-year forward EPS growth is near +40%, against a one-year change in forward P/E near -20%.

Since June the largest valuation hits landed on the stocks with the strongest earnings: EU semis, Korea's Kospi, US AI infrastructure, AEJ AI hardware and the SOX are down roughly 20% to 30% in dollar terms. The AI-enabled revenues and AI productivity baskets re-rated up roughly 15% to 25%.

S&P 500 earnings growth peaked near 40% y/y, about three times nominal GDP growth, and Goldman forecasts it fading to about 10% by 2027 (read off the chart, approximate). Goldman says the level of earnings stays healthy enough to support equity carry relative to bonds.

Goldman's case for equities over credit rests on long-run outperformance on a volatility-matched basis since 1994 and on the Carry Opportunity Indicator, which is near its lowest since the GFC. Goldman reads low risk premia as poor asymmetry for carry trades and more vulnerability to growth and rate shocks.

Since January 2022 the equity-over-credit gap is widest where AI money went: the Nasdaq 100 is up about 60% versus USD IG tech credit on a beta-adjusted basis and the S&P about 45% versus HY. The Russell 2000 versus HY is about flat.

The Tech sector equity weight is above Tech Bubble levels and TMT is close to half of US equity market cap. Goldman's hedges, based on 15 TMT drawdowns above 10% since 1950, are real assets, value over growth, and Treasuries.

Goldman warns that being underinvested late cycle can be costly, since equities usually perform well up until the bull market peak. It also notes that the speed of bond yield increases matters, and that sticky inflation and fiscal concerns are hard for equities to digest.

Goldman's base case is a return to Goldilocks: inflation normalizes, real growth stays near trend and the hawkish monetary-policy shock fades. The deck says the stagflation risk to 60/40 portfolios has moderated.

The author sides with Goldman on credit, citing tight spreads plus heavy AI issuance, but is skeptical on equities. The author cites the risk appetite break below zero, a December hike still priced and two megacaps punished for cash burn as resembling 2022.
Convertible issuance has increased because of AI funding needs, and Goldman likes converts as an equity-like bond for late-cycle backdrops.

sector_views.rationale: Overweight on 3-month and 12-month horizons, supported by healthy earnings levels and a roughly 20% fall in forward P/E.
Underweight on both horizons because the Carry Opportunity Indicator is near its lowest since the GFC and equities have historically outperformed credit.
Moves to overweight over 12 months. 10Y bonds returned 3.9% on average in past TMT drawdowns.
Overweight for the next three months.
Staying long equities means being long Tech, whose weight is above Tech Bubble levels. Goldman suggests hedging with real assets, value and Treasuries.
Valuations fell roughly 20% to 30% in dollar terms since June despite double-digit earnings contributions. The deck presents this as a de-rating, not a stance change.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 earnings growth peaked at roughly 40% y/y, about three times nominal GDP growth, per Goldman's chart (read off the chart, approximate). Goldman's own forecast has it fading to about 10% by 2027.
Consensus-based equity carry (dividend yield plus forward EPS growth) peaks near 40% and fades toward 20%, which Goldman calls still plenty compared to a 10Y near 5%.
Alphabet is reported by the author to have had its worst day ever and Amazon to have fallen as cash burn rose this week. No EPS or revenue figures are given in the document.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied odds of a December hike remain high even after this week's Fed meeting trimmed about 10bps off 2027 terminal pricing. This keeps pressure on risk appetite.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight global equities and underweight credit on 3-month and 12-month horizons, with overweight cash for 3 months.
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings support equity carry, and credit offers poor risk premia versus equities with the same AI exposure.
trade_ideas.risk: Sticky inflation and rising yields are hard for equities to digest, and the 2022 analog is the exception in Goldman's PC2 chart.

trade_ideas.description: Shift to overweight 10-year government bonds over a 12-month view.
trade_ideas.rationale: 10Y bonds returned 3.9% on average in past TMT drawdowns of more than 10%.
trade_ideas.risk: The speed of bond yield increases matters, and 10Y yields are near 5.00%.

trade_ideas.description: Hedge long Tech exposure with real assets (commodities, gold), value over growth, low-vol and high-dividend stocks, and Treasuries.
trade_ideas.rationale: In 15 TMT drawdowns of more than 10% since 1950, the S&P GSCI rose 23.7% on average, gold 9.8%, and value beat growth by 17%.

trade_ideas.description: Own convertible bonds as an equity-like bond for late-cycle backdrops.
trade_ideas.rationale: Convertible issuance has increased due to AI funding needs, and Goldman likes the equity-like profile.

risk_factors: Inflation fails to cool, with WTI around $100 and elevated oil prices called structural by Shell's CEO.
The Fed hikes in December (odds around 80%) and the 10Y yield stays near 5.00%.
The current monetary-policy factor trough tracks the 2022 path, the one exception to the average recovery.
Tech concentration above Tech Bubble levels, with capex-driven earnings the market no longer trusts to last.
Hyperscaler cash burn and AI debt issuance, with tight spreads, widen credit and data-center CDS stress.
The 60/40 portfolio may be in an inflation trap where bonds no longer hedge stocks.
charts_described: Goldman growth score has run well above zero all year, while the policy score has rolled over sharply and Goldman's forecast has it falling further below zero into 2027.

Risk Appetite Indicator, split into principal components, shows the Monetary policy factor (PC2) collapsing, with a 'Middle East war' label on the latest leg lower after a brief 'central bank put' phase.
PC2 trough chart across 11 troughs since 2000 shows the current line tracking the 2022 path more closely than the average.
Valuation chart shows dividend yield plus one-year forward EPS growth near +40% against one-year change in forward P/E near -20%.
Decomposition since June shows tech hardware baskets down roughly 20% to 30% in dollar terms and AI-enabled baskets up roughly 15% to 25%.
Consensus-based equity carry peaks near 40% and fades toward 20%.
Volatility-matched comparisons since 1994 show equity beating credit in TMT, S&P versus US IG and Russell versus HY.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's Carry Opportunity Indicator (EM, sovereign and corporate credit, FX, equity vol, yield curve) is near its lowest since the GFC, signaling poor asymmetry for carry trades.
Goldman prefers to balance equities with bonds, gold and low vol instead of credit. Low vol and dividend aristocrats versus IG ('bond proxies') are up only around 10% since January 2022.
Tech sector equity weight is above Tech Bubble levels and TMT is close to half of US equity market cap, above the 2000 peak.
IG spreads have blown back out to recent wide, and hyperscaler credit, including Meta SPV bonds and data-center CDS, sold off in the author's account of this week.
geopolitical: A 'Middle East war' label marks the latest leg lower in Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator, after a brief 'central bank put' phase.
Shell's CEO is cited as calling elevated oil prices 'structural', with WTI pinned around $100.
cross_bank_references: Goldman partner Mark Wilson made the 'stagflation is priced, Goldilocks is coming' pitch last month.
Goldman's commodity team last week argued that the 60/40 needs a third leg.
Bloomberg's Simon White argues the 60/40 portfolio is caught in an inflation trap where bonds no longer hedge stocks.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's base case is that inflation normalizes, real growth stays near trend, the hawkish monetary-policy shock fades and equities are carried higher by earnings. Sharp drops in the monetary-policy factor have usually been buying opportunities.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising yields from sticky inflation and fiscal concerns are hard for equities to digest. The current trough tracks 2022, the one exception, while a December hike is about 80% priced and the 10Y is near 5.00%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's bull case needs a renewed decline in inflation momentum. Continued sticky inflation with yields near 5.00% would break it.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities have historically outperformed credit, and the Carry Opportunity Indicator near its lowest since the GFC says credit pays little for the risk.
tension_points.bear_case: The author doubts equities can hold up if bonds and credit are right, as stocks ignored bond and credit signals all year while a risk appetite gauge broke below zero.

tension_points.bull_case: The de-rating keeps the equity case alive because earnings level stays healthy and supports equity carry relative to bonds.
tension_points.bear_case: The market has stopped paying for capex-driven earnings it does not trust to last, with Alphabet and Amazon punished for cash burn.
